question: Separate in-kind corporate gifts from the 2% excess: for Part II recipients, read Schedule M (noncash contributions by type, columns (b)/(c)) and Part VIII 1g, and recompute the large-donor share of 1f and the net DAF share on a cash-only basis (1f - 1g, excess scaled by cash share)
conclusion_affected: Size of the large-donor share of 1f (pooled 18.5% Part II) and the net DAF share for >=$100m recipients
rationale: Four in-kind relief charities (Good360, Feeding America, Direct Relief, Americares) hold 23.5% of the weighted Part II excess; the pooled large-donor share falls only to 16.0% when noncash-heavy recipients are dropped, but the >=$100m band (22.0%) is driven by product donations

question: Do recipients put DAF grants inside Schedule A Part II line 5? Take the Part II recipients whose net DAF share exceeds 100% (6.9% weighted) or rises by >10 points after netting, and compare their top-50 DAF-weighted Schedule I receipts with line 5 and Schedule A Part VI narrative (unusual grants, attribution notes)
conclusion_affected: Whether 1f net of the 2% excess keeps DAF grants in the denominator as the instructions imply
rationale: The instructions exempt grants from 170(b)(1)(A)(vi) organisations (98.4% of top-50 DAF grants) from the 2% limit, yet net shares >100% rise from 5.0% to 6.9% after netting (e.g. Grounded Solutions Network: $11.2m numerator, 1f $19.8m, cy excess $10.7m), suggesting some filers attribute DAF grants to donors

question: Line 5 = 0 diagnostic: for the 500 Part II filers (46.1% weighted) reporting no excess over 2%, test whether zero reflects no large donor or non-computation, using Part II line 1 year-to-year volatility, First5Years170Ind, PublicSupportCY170Pct and the size of the largest Schedule I grant each received from any 990 filer in the TEOS index
conclusion_affected: Median large-donor share (1.8%) and medians of the net DAF share
rationale: A zero line 5 is implausible for many small organisations where 2% of five-year support is a few thousand dollars; if a share are non-computed, the median large-donor share is understated

question: Apply the Schedule A excess netting to the Chariot size-matched comparison (recipients with average 1h-1d-1e of $50-200m a year) to see whether the 2.6-point gap below Chariot's 12.6% closes on a sub-2% contributions basis
conclusion_affected: Filings vs Chariot 12.6% DAF share of total giving
rationale: Netting the excess raises the Part II pooled DAF share by about 2.5 points (11.4% to 13.9%) and the $25-100m band from 12.4% to 14.5%, which is the size of the reported gap; both inputs are already cached so this is a join

question: Multi-year denominator: use Schedule A Part II line 1 five-year columns (and Part VIII 1f of FY2021-22 returns from the TEOS index) to compute the DAF share against average contributions, removing timing mismatches between DAF grant years and lumpy recipient revenue
conclusion_affected: Share of recipients with DAF share >100% and the size of the line-5 window mismatch
rationale: Part II line 1(e) equals Part VIII 1h exactly (weighted quartiles 1.00), so the prior four columns give a filer-reported contributions history at no extra fetch cost; the cy and avg allocations of line 5 already give large-donor shares 2.5 points apart (pooled 18.5% vs 16.0%, Part II)
